note: depends_on may name tasks in docs/METTHEW/tasks.json (M-xx) or a sibling here (S-xx). Nothing in this file is built; every entry is a recorded goal with the gate that would decide it is real.

F.name: GRAFT -- social problems answered by sharing shards
F.gates: S-01 -> S-06 are independent; S-01 first
F.one_line: ship the piece, not the platform: content-addressed, offline, deterministic, provenance-carrying units that a school, a tenant, a small charity or a creator can run without an account

tasks.title: Second-life device kit: three offline shards that run on hardware already owned
tasks.problem: device divide: 21M US students lack home internet (tier D, 2026-04-09) while 62 Mt of e-waste is generated a year with 22.3% properly recycled (tier C, 2025-02-26)

evidence.claim: 21 million students lack home internet access

grafts.piece: a runnable shard whose tiers prove one hash

tasks.deliverable: three shard bundles (a reader, a maths drill, an offline reference) each declaring tier 0 as handheld, plus one run-anywhere page and a cold-start measurement
tasks.acceptance: each bundle is <= 2097152 bytes and <= 24 files, passes tools/metthew_validate.py, and a cold start on the weakest available machine is measured and recorded rather than estimated
tasks.risk: software that fits the hardware still needs a human to hand it over; without a school or library partner this is a shelf artefact

tasks.title: Tenant answer packet: deterministic form assembly, never advice
tasks.problem: civil justice gap: 92% of low-income Americans received no or insufficient help for civil legal problems (LSC, tier B); working precedents assemble forms rather than advise (MADE 2025-10-15, tier B)

evidence.claim: 92% of low-income Americans did not receive any or enough legal help for civil legal problems
MADE helps self-represented Massachusetts tenants prepare the seven forms they need
Tenant Power Toolkit fills eviction responses

grafts.piece: refusal discipline for a stale declaration

tasks.deliverable: one county's answer packet: 12 questions, a dated rules table (rules_version), generated forms with computed filing dates, and a sha256 of the produced packet
tasks.acceptance: the packet hash is identical on two hosts; a rules_version older than a declared horizon is REFUSED rather than answered; a legal-aid reviewer signs off that the output is forms, not advice
tasks.risk: stale law is worse than no tool; the horizon check is the whole safety property and it must be the first thing built

tasks.title: Companion safety kernel: on-device persona, enumerated intents, crisis protocol, local record
tasks.problem: AI companions now face statute before substrate: California signed 13 youth-facing AI bills on 2026-09-10 (tier A) and New York required a self-harm detection protocol from 2025-11-05 (tier C); UNICEF and the European Parliament both published 2026 briefs (tier A)

evidence.claim: 13 bills targeting online and AI-related risks to children, incl. companion chatbots and K-12 pupil data
New York operators must implement a reasonable self-harm detection protocol from 2025-11-05
six-jurisdiction policy brief on AI companions and children's rights
European Parliament briefing on AI companions

grafts.piece: hash-chained record of what was said, when

tasks.deliverable: a persona card schema, an enumerated intent set, a crisis-protocol state machine with a named human escalation target, local-only logging, and an evidence pack mapping each control to the bill that asks for it
tasks.acceptance: a test proves the model cannot emit an intent outside the enum; the crisis path is exercised end to end with a recorded escalation; no network egress occurs during a session (proved by a negative control that fails if any egress is attempted)
tasks.risk: crisis handling is clinical and legal work; shipping it without a named human escalation partner is worse than shipping nothing, and the evidence pack is not legal advice

tasks.title: Records backlog bench: triage, redaction review, appeal skeleton, hash-chained log
tasks.problem: public-records backlog: about 340,000 overdue FOIA requests at federal agencies as of 2025-09-30 (NYT 2026-07-30, tier C); GAO has documented the pattern (tier A/B)

evidence.claim: federal agencies accumulated a backlog of nearly 340,000 overdue requests as of 2025-09-30
FOIA backlogs hinder transparency and accountability

tasks.deliverable: ingest of one agency's response set, deterministic triage queue, redaction review UI, appeal-letter skeleton with statutory dates computed from a dated table, and a hash-chained action log
tasks.acceptance: on a seeded 200-page set, redaction recall and precision are both measured, with a clean-page control that must not be redacted; the appeal dates are checked against the statute table for 3 worked examples
outside_repo: .bcc_audit/03_tooling/behavior_trace.py and process_corpus.py live in C:/Users/clint, NOT in this repo; the bench would import that discipline, so it is a real external dependency rather than a graftable path
tasks.risk: a redaction false negative is an irreversible disclosure; the tool must be review-first and must publish its measured false-negative rate, not just its accuracy

tasks.title: Small-org evidence pack: the artefact an insurer asks for, run quarterly
tasks.problem: small organisations are the ransomware economy's main customer: 32% of surveyed charities faced an attack and over 2 in 5 report limited or no preparation (tier D, 2026); 17 registered nonprofit ransomware victims in January 2026 alone (tier C)

evidence.claim: 17 registered ransomware victims in January 2026 alone
32% of charities faced a cyber attack; over 2 in 5 report limited or no preparation

tasks.deliverable: one pack script plus a report template: secret scan, dependency scan, backup integrity check, access-review checklist, each with a hash-chained receipt and a non-empty 'what we could not check' section
tasks.acceptance: the pack runs twice on the same machine and the receipts chain; the report refuses to print a clean bill when a component was skipped (the skipped component is named); a fixture repo with a planted secret is caught
tasks.risk: an evidence pack describes a machine's state, not the absence of an attacker; presenting it as assurance is the failure mode to avoid

tasks.title: Provenance stamp for creators: content-addressed lineage, verifiable offline
tasks.problem: attribution: AI-generated material competes with human work and a creator's only defence is provable lineage; platforms are not obliged to provide it
tasks.evidence_gap: no external statistic was recorded for this one in the 2026-11-01 searches; the problem statement (AI material competes with human work and platforms owe creators no lineage) is qualitative here. Re-search before this task is scheduled, and treat the local manifest fields as the ANSWER, not as evidence of the problem.
tasks.deliverable: stamp <file> --author <key> and verify <file>, both offline: a sidecar lineage record naming the inputs by hash and the author by public key
tasks.acceptance: stamp then verify round-trips with no network; a file whose bytes are altered fails verification; a sidecar whose lineage names a missing input is refused
tasks.risk: a stamp proves lineage, not authorship of an idea; it cannot stop a plagiarist and must not be marketed as if it could
